summary:
LFM2-24B-A2B: 7 parts passed out of 21 screens used. Six are expert sets within one layer; one is a whole block.

Passed parts:
1. Factual recall, L37: 12 experts [57,8,60,40,30,7,35,54,9,18,33,32]. facts -.21.
2. Factual recall, L36: 10 experts [45,1,56,39,46,4,42,62,37,34]. facts -.156.
3. Factual recall, L35: 14 experts [53,15,46,43,58,4,0,11,10,12,30,36,40,59]. facts -.151.
4. Roman-numeral conversion, L30: 8 experts [10,14,30,16,58,11,17,18]. roman -.407.
5. Subject-verb agreement, L30: 6 experts [36,49,53,31,58,19]. SVA -.232.
6. Month sequence, L13: 6 experts [48,8,2,62,1,24]. month -.518.
7. Chinese numerals, whole block L29: chinese -.725.

Recipe that worked:
- Sweep single-layer blocks to locate the skill.
- In that layer, scan attribution and routing for the target and for the skills that tend to leak.
- Keep the target's top experts and remove experts attributed to leaking skills; 6–14 experts.

Mechanisms found but not screenable (each hits several skills):
- L33 expert 12 is a successor hub (month/weekday/math).
- L38 expert 36 is a numeric-answer writer (math/chinese).
- Digit writers: L37 expert 23 and L39 experts 63/53/21.
- L39 expert 12 is an antonym writer that also drops its control.
- L30 heads [21,3,29,26,5] drop facts -.40, but general_text drops too.
- L14 heads [1,4,29,31] drop SVA -.23, but month just exceeds its limit.
- L38 heads 12 and 14 are critical.

Negative results:
- Code, multilingual and en_fr translation did not localize under any part kind tried.
- Calendar skills are coupled across layers, and early month experts also hurt antonym.
- The skill cap blocked new tests.

summary:
LFM2-24B-A2B run: 27 parts passed the screen out of 30 screened. 26 are routed-expert pools of 2-7 experts in one layer; one is a group of 4 attention heads. Caveat: the 17 chinese_numeral passes rest on a base score of only .033, so their large relative drops come from very few correct items. The month and antonym passes stand on bases of .75 and .52.

**What passed (screened drop on the target skill)**
- **Chinese numerals, 16 expert pools** in L6, L8, L12, L14, L17, L18, L19, L20, L21, L24, L25, L28, L29, L32 and L35:
  - drops from .235 to .89, strongest at L12 [11,28,52,60,36];
  - controls moved at most ±.26.
- **Chinese numerals, attention heads** at L22 [26,18,17,24]: drop .764.
- **Month successor, 8 expert pools**, all with controls within ±.05:
  - L2 [62,37,30]: .361
  - L3 [4,8,15]: .241
  - L8 [11,63,44]: .186
  - L10 [24,44,42,4]: .327
  - L11 [7,28]: .401
  - L14 [21,24,44,12]: .359
  - L16 [45,4,51,41,21]: .426
  - L21 [62,11,42,22,55]: .271
- **Antonym, 2 expert pools**:
  - L7 [23,46,42,38]: .344
  - L8 [14,25,17]: .359

**Methods that worked**
- **Attribution plus exclusion:** take one layer's top-attribution experts for the skill, then drop experts shared with weekday, month, a_an or facts.
- **Splitting leaky pools:** splitting a pool that hit two skills isolated:
  - the L7 antonym carriers;
  - month-only pools at L3, L8 and L11;
  - a month pool at L2 without e28, the en_fr-routed expert behind an en_fr side effect of .21.
- **Routing selectivity:** this found the L8 antonym pool. It only worked in early layers.

**What failed or never localized**
- **Failed screens:** L9 chinese and L20 month pools lost to random same-size sets. A trimmed 4-expert L2 pool [9,13,21,12] for antonym also lost to a random set.
- **Routing leaders that did nothing when ablated:** antonym in L13-L30, code at L33 (e55, 89x), multilingual at L38 (e20, 82x) and L34, and math at L33. All were at most .035.
- **Weight-only reading:** L39 experts whose output weights point at non-Latin scripts or code tokens moved multilingual and code by at most .06.
- **Blocks:** every single-layer block I ablated was broad.
- **Dense-MLP families:** month families of 16-64 neurons at L0/L1 always drop weekday .46-.53 too.
- **Head groups:** month heads at L6, L22 and L26 also drop weekday.
- **Skills I couldn't isolate:**
  - roman: L15 e30 also drops chinese.
  - SVA: its control swings ±.4-.9.
  - weekday: its control base is .004.
  - a_an: its control drops together with the target.
  - facts outside L35-L37: at most .097.
  - en_fr: only moves with broad parts.

summary:
LFM2-24B-A2B session: 8 new parts passed the screen, all whole-expert sets chosen from the weights and checked by ablation.
1) L31 expert 12: weekday-name writer (5.0x weekday-unembedding energy). weekday_successor drop .607, random draws 0.
2) L36 experts [47,11,3]: weekday-name writers. weekday_successor drop .24, control -.005, random draws ≤0. e47 was found because it leaked weekday collateral into the L36 geography set.
3) L34 experts [9,55]: calendar-name writers. month_successor drop .202.
4) L18 experts [11,12,41,43]: non-English/CJK routing experts. chinese_numeral drop .49. Weak: very low base score (0.033), one random draw at .18.
5) L37, 16 experts: country/capital writers. facts drop .183.
6) L35, 20 experts: country/capital writers. facts drop .173. Thin margin: random draws reached .16 and .152.
7) L36, 22 experts: country/capital writers. facts drop .154, only just over the .15 threshold.
8) L38, 16 experts: French/Spanish/German function-word writers. en_fr_translation drop .173, its control .003.

Failed screen: an L31 country/capital set of 24 experts dropped facts .159 on the search half but failed the held-out check.

Recipe: score each expert's down-projection by its energy on a category's unembedding rows (tied embeddings times embedding_norm) against random tokens, minus its energy on competing categories. Take the top experts in one late layer, then use the same per-expert energies to find and remove members that leak into other skills.

What failed:
- Math and code: no single-layer expert set moved them, whether picked from the unembedding, router rows, routing scans or attribution. They look redundant across the top-4 routing.
- Hub experts L33 e12 (month/weekday/math) and L38 e36 (math/numerals) are not separable.
- L39 sets cause broad damage.
- Blocks L33 and L37 were not selective.
- L0 dense-MLP clusters gave noisy effects.
- Attention head groups damaged most skills at once.
- Router-row adjective sets in L10-12 did not move antonym.
- The strongest weekday-routed L23 experts (e1/e37) improved weekday when ablated rather than hurting it.
- Weekday writers at L32, L33, L37 and L38 had no weekday effect.
- New skills could not be defined because the agent skill cap was reached.

summary:
LFM2-24B-A2B: no part passed this run. I used 2 of 6 screens (both failed), ran 29 ablations and 4 attribution scans. I couldn't define a new skill to test the best lead because the agent skill cap (8) is full.

**1. L39 math answer writers (best lead, failed its screen on one leak).**
- The set is L39 experts [63, 22, 58, 53]. Expert 63 is a number writer: its down-projection puts about 8x the median energy into the number-token directions, and its top direction writes 20, 30, 50, 25, 40 and the digits. Experts 58 and 53 are the next number writers, and expert 22 is math-attributed.
- In the screen, math dropped .281 while random same-size parts dropped about 0.
- It failed only because chinese_numeral, also a skill that outputs numbers, dropped .132 against a limit of .094. Antonym moved .056.
- Expert 63 is needed for both skills: without it, math falls to .096. Adding more number writers (7 experts) raised chinese_numeral to .358 but math only to .295.
- Next step: test it on a numeric skill that doesn't compete with chinese_numeral, or free a skill slot for a number-word-to-digits test.

**2. Digit-copy attention heads (a test through each head's value/output weights) are hubs that work together.**
- L30 GQA group 6 (heads 24 to 27) dropped math .585, but also roman_numeral .957, month .952, weekday .806 and facts .255.
- L38 heads 0, 2, 8 and 11 (scores about 5) together dropped math .205 and month .286. Ablating either of their two head groups alone dropped math only about .05.

**3. Broad hubs to avoid:**
- L38 expert 36 has huge math attribution but writes the start-of-text tokens. With experts 38 and 3 it dropped math .65 and chinese_numeral .95.
- The L5 [34, 33, 56] and L10 [25, 23, 2] expert sets dropped a_an_article about .8, but its own control by .9 to .97.
- The whole L39 block damages every skill.

**4. Inert when ablated (under .04 on their targets):**
- Code writers: L33 expert 14 writes "(" variants, plus L32 and L15 expert sets.
- French function-word writers: L36 expert 2 writes la/une, L37 expert 53 writes au/à, L38 expert 18 writes d'/l'.
- Roman-numeral writer sets at L36 and L38, and the roman_numeral experts with the highest attribution at L4 and L5.
- Antonym experts at L11 with the highest attribution.
- Number writers at L34 and L35, even though they matched the math attribution.

In this model, code and French look spread across many experts. The math bottleneck sits in L39 and the L30 and L38 attention, and it is shared with the numeral and ordinal-sequence tasks.

summary: Short run (about 10 min). I read expert weights two ways: (1) the energy of each expert's w2 output inside a category's unembedding subspace (digits, code, French, German), and (2) router gate routing of ffn_norm-scaled token embeddings. Digit structure is clear in the weights: output-side digit-writer experts at L32 [8,10,11,22,60,61], L35 [49,63,46,61,4] (49 is about 6x baseline) and L37 [27,23], and input-side digit-routed experts at L2 [20,52,32], L3 [30,13,52,17,37], L4 [21,4,16] and L5 [18,24,20,49,7]. Code and language subspaces gave no separable experts (selectivity near 0). Causally, none of the digit sets moved math (all |drop| under 0.01), so math has high margin or redundancy in this MoE. L35 digit writers moved only the weekday/roman controls (+0.25/+0.18). L3 digit-routed experts dropped month_successor .161 and weekday_successor .149, but the controls swung hugely (antonym ctrl -0.68, chinese ctrl -1.29), so the effect is not selective. L5 digit-routed experts improved chinese_numeral (-0.40). No screens were spent because no candidate looked able to pass. Lesson for teammates: weight-identified digit experts on LFM2-24B-A2B are real lexical routers or writers, but single-layer sets of 5-6 do not bottleneck math. Try multi-layer blocks or larger cross-layer unions, or skills with a lower base margin.
